symptom: A project built by an older mxcli stays unmergeable after the property-set completion shipped: `mx diff` still throws `Objects with ID … of type Microflows$RestOperationCallAction do not have the same properties` (ErrorHandlingType missing), and Projects$ModuleSettings, ChangeActionItem.Attribute and the rest stay incomplete even after re-running the whole MDL corpus (16 of 64 affected units rewritten) (ako/mxcli#1097)
cause: Reach, not elision. The suspicion was that normalizePropertySets running before canon.Reconcile made a rewrite of an incomplete unit compare equal and get elided; measured, it does not — canon.Equal compares the canonical form strictly, so the normalized bytes (with the key) differ from the stored ones (without it) and the write lands. The gaps live in units NO statement rewrites: module settings, documents whose script is not re-run, and any unit a statement reaches only by reading
file: `modelsdk/mpr/writer_property_sets.go` (`Writer.CompleteStoredPropertySets`, `Reader.StoredPropertySetGaps`, `normalizePropertySetsFor` shared with `normalizePropertySets`), `cmd/mxcli/cmd_fix_property_sets.go` (`mxcli fix property-sets [--dry-run]`); tests `modelsdk/mpr/writer_property_set_repair_test.go` (incl. `TestStoredUnitMissingAKeyIsCompletedByAnyRewrite`, the measurement of the premise), `cmd/mxcli/cmd_fix_property_sets_test.go`
insight: **Measure the premise before building the bypass.** The brief asked for an elision bypass; a ten-line writer test (stored unit missing a table key, UpdateRawUnit of the same bytes, read the file) showed the write lands, so the repair goes through the ORDINARY update path — Reconcile, the storage-GUID guard and every other guard — and needed no bypass at all. A write-path change that would have been justified by a false premise is the one that breaks rule 2 of 'Writes Are Conditional'. **A per-write fix only reaches what is written**: anything normalized at the choke point needs a sweep for the units already stored, or the fix is invisible on every existing project. **Decide on property NAMES, not bytes**: the sweep compares per-node key sets (by containment path — normalization never reorders a list), so it is idempotent by construction and a second run offers nothing. **The control is a Studio Pro-authored project**: `fix property-sets --dry-run` on testdata/pedapp (11.13.0), expr-checker (11.6.6) and testapp-views (11.14.0) reports 0 units — a table row adding a key Studio Pro does not write would show up there first
